# Lanson Live API — Documentation for AI assistants

Last updated: 2026-11-08

> LansonAI is the Voice Context Layer for Live Speech. Lanson Live API is its
> developer-facing speech capability. Each entry links to
> the canonical page served by the docs site.
>
> Base URL: https://docs.lansonai.com
> Raw Markdown for any page: https://docs.lansonai.com/raw/docs/<path>.md
> OpenAPI spec (Recorded API): https://audio.lansonai.com/openapi.json
>
> Design principle: Human-readable + Agent-readable + Schema-accurate.
> Pages are organized by "what a developer wants to build", not by internal
> technology names. Technology concepts (Trinity Engine, StableStream™, LiveFinal™) are
> explained only after a developer has chosen a capability.

## Brand and technology

- LansonAI: company and platform — Voice Context Layer for Live Speech.
- Lanson Live: speech model brand; model name `lanson-live-1`. Lanson Live API exposes the capability to developers, without a model-selection step.
- Trinity Engine: core engine for multi-model orchestration, speech processing, and context coordination. Not a selectable model.
- StableStream™: core technology for continuous, stable, readable live text. Not an event type.
- LiveFinal™: progressive correction and segment-finalization mechanism. The public Realtime endpoint currently delivers a single completed result per successfully processed utterance, with optional refinement applied before delivery.
- Lanson Live App: end-user live speech product; distinct from Lanson Live API. Other product lines include Lanson Flow, Lanson Reception, and Lanson Podcast.
- HTTP `model` is an optional compatibility field; omit it in new examples. If a client requires a name, use `lanson-live-1`. Existing request values need not change. Do not expose provider/worker names as public model brands.
- Preserve endpoint URLs, request field names, and event identifiers exactly as documented. Do not fabricate partial/revision/final event types or treat manual flush as an implemented finalization command.

## Why Lanson Live differs from conventional transcription APIs

> **AI Review is not the ASR model's built-in language understanding.**
>
> Lanson Live uses a separate language reasoning model to review each transcription candidate against the conversation's context. This happens inside the real-time transcription pipeline, before the completed text is delivered.
>
> The speech recognition model identifies the words. The reasoning model evaluates them. StableStream™ makes it possible to deliver the reviewed result as the first committed transcript.

1. **Three Distinct Architectural Layers (Not Just ASR Internal Language Modeling)**:
   - **Layer 1 — Speech Recognition Model (ASR)**: Predicts candidate words from audio signals, phonetic patterns, hotwords, and a very narrow, sound-bound local window. Conventional STT APIs stop here; their "language understanding" is merely the acoustic decoder's internal statistical language model.
   - **Layer 2 — Separate Language Reasoning Model (Lanson's In-Pipeline LLM Review)**: After ASR produces a candidate transcript, a separate language reasoning model (LLM) evaluates that candidate with human-like semantic comprehension across multi-turn conversation history, domain context, and phonetic clues. Crucially, Lanson Live harnesses the reasoning model's deep semantic comprehension **but constrains its objective strictly to faithfully recovering the speaker's verbatim words** (zero paraphrasing). The model does not lose its reasoning capability just because it is not performing intent analysis, task planning, or tool calling—instead, 100% of its reasoning power is focused on contextual speech disambiguation.
   - **Layer 3 — Real-Time Delivery Orchestration (`StableStream™` & `LiveFinal™`)**: Establishes the segment boundary that allows **both** the ASR recognition model and the separate language reasoning model to finish their work *before* the first committed transcript is delivered.
2. **The Hard Problem — Real-Time AI Refinement & The Structural Price Paid**:
   - Post-recording AI cleanup is trivial because offline models have the full recording and no latency clock. Running a separate language reasoning model in real time while the speaker is still talking requires paying a structural price that conventional streaming STT APIs refuse to pay: **giving up unreviewed, word-by-word provisional draft streaming (`partial` tokens)**.
   - Conventional streaming STT optimizes for time-to-first-phonetic-token, pushing incomplete ASR guesses across the wire before a sentence has semantic context. Even its `is_final` flag only means the ASR acoustic decoder closed its buffer—without review by a separate reasoning model.
   - Lanson Live (**StableStream™**) deliberately collects speech into a bounded segment window so that ASR recognition + LLM semantic review both run *inside* the pipeline before a single immutable completed utterance crosses the **LiveFinal™** delivery boundary.
3. **Dynamic Segment Sizing by Scenario Latency Tolerance**:
   - Because Lanson Live trades meaningless draft flicker for a bounded dual-model window, segment duration is an architectural lever matched to the scenario's latency tolerance: `2–4s` for latency-sensitive voice turn-taking, `5–10s` for live conversations and meetings, and `12s+` for broadcast caption feeds.
4. **Why Naive External LLMs Make Live Transcripts Worse — And How Lanson's Pipeline Prevents It**:
   - Naively bolting an unconstrained general-purpose LLM onto real-time speech fragments often makes transcripts *worse*: short 2–4s clips trigger LLM hallucinations, grammar paraphrasing/rewriting of speaker intent, over-correction of valid speech, and inconsistent entity spelling across turns.
   - Lanson Live solves this through its disciplined four-stage pipeline philosophy:
     - **Bounded Semantic Window (`StableStream™`)**: Gives the ASR model and reasoning model coherent utterance segments rather than sub-word acoustic shards.
     - **Human-Like Multi-Turn Semantic Memory (`Conversation Context`)**: Carries distilled entities, names, and domain terms across turns to overcome the narrow acoustic window of ASR and the short duration of real-time slices.
     - **Restrained, Speaker-Faithful Disambiguation (`Context-aware Refinement`)**: Combines phonetic plausibility with semantic conversation evidence, enforces **Zero Paraphrasing**, skips ultra-short fragments that lack disambiguation evidence (while retaining them as future context), and leaves already-accurate recognition untouched.
     - **Single-Handoff Delivery Boundary (`LiveFinal™` & `AI-ready Transcripts`)**: Emits one completed event per utterance with `text`, preserved `raw_text`, `utterance_index`, `transcript.state` (`stable`), `transcript.correction_applied`, and `transcript.safe_for_downstream`—with deterministic fallback to `raw_text` if refinement fails.

## AI-Native Transcription

- [Overview](/docs/ai-native-transcription): The real-time AI refinement dilemma, why Lanson Live pays the segment-window price conventional STT refuses to pay, why naive LLMs degrade live captions, and the 3-way paradigm comparison (Conventional STT vs. DIY STT+LLM vs. Lanson Live).
- [StableStream™](/docs/ai-native-transcription/stablestream): Why trading word-by-word draft flicker for scenario-tuned segment windows (`2–4s`, `5–10s`, `12s+`) makes real-time AI review possible.
- [Context-aware Refinement](/docs/ai-native-transcription/context-aware-refinement): Controlling the double-edged sword of AI in live speech—phonetic plausibility, speaker-faithful zero paraphrasing, disciplined non-intervention, and deterministic fallback.
- [Conversation Context](/docs/ai-native-transcription/conversation-context): Solving the short-window paradox by pairing intra-segment audio windows with rolling cross-utterance conversational memory.
- [LiveFinal™](/docs/ai-native-transcription/livefinal): Placing the delivery boundary after in-pipeline review so applications receive one immutable completed handoff instead of draft-and-patch rewrites.
- [AI-ready Transcripts](/docs/ai-native-transcription/ai-ready-transcripts): Structured events, utterance ordering (`utterance_index`), delivery state, and readiness signals (`safe_for_downstream`) for downstream AI agents.

## Realtime Voice Context

- [Overview](/docs/realtime): Lanson Live API Realtime inputs, completed text, optional correction/translation, and technology boundaries.
- [Realtime Quickstart](/docs/realtime/quickstart): Python, Node.js, and browser connection examples; supply real PCM audio instead of placeholders.
- [Connection Lifecycle](/docs/realtime/connection-lifecycle): Connect → configure → stream audio → receive events → close/reconnect; state machine, timeouts, idle/session limits.
- [Audio Input](/docs/realtime/audio-input): PCM, sample rate, channels, chunk size, supported formats, chunk/latency tradeoffs.
- [Transcript Lifecycle](/docs/realtime/transcript-lifecycle): VAD → recognition → optional refinement → one completed event per successful utterance. No partial or later-revision protocol on this endpoint.
- [Realtime Translation](/docs/realtime/realtime-translation): Source/translation mapping, language config, language switching, latency behavior.
- [Session Configuration](/docs/realtime/session-configuration): language and session-level options; config timing (connect vs runtime).
- [Handling Interruptions & Silence](/docs/realtime/interruptions-silence): silence, pause, session continuation, VAD / end-of-speech behavior.

## API Reference

- [Overview](/docs/api-reference): Base URL, REST / WebSocket, versioning (`/v1/...`); per-endpoint template.
- [Realtime API](/docs/api-reference/realtime-api): WebSocket endpoint; connection URL and query params; auth; message format (JSON).
- [Client Messages](/docs/api-reference/client-messages): All client → Lanson messages; field schemas.
- [Server Events](/docs/api-reference/server-events): Exact Lanson Live API event types, correction metadata, translation association, and ordering.
- [Segment Transcription](/docs/api-reference/segment-transcription): `POST /v1/audio/transcriptions` — synchronous multipart client-VAD transcription.
- [Batch Jobs](/docs/api-reference/batch-jobs): Async batch transcription jobs — enqueue and poll.
- [Languages & Models](/docs/api-reference/languages): Lanson Live model brand (`lanson-live-1`), language behavior, and optional HTTP compatibility field; no model selection required.
- [Language Detection](/docs/api-reference/language-detection): `POST /v1/audio/language-detection` — detect language of a short clip (≤20s) without transcription; use when the language is unknown.
- [Errors](/docs/api-reference/errors): HTTP error codes; WebSocket error events; payload schema; common errors and triage.
- [Rate Limits](/docs/api-reference/rate-limits): Concurrency, requests, session duration; per-plan limits; over-limit behavior.
- [Admin API](/docs/api-reference/admin): Key provisioning, revocation, plan catalog (internal operators and dashboards only).

## Notes for coding agents

- The Realtime WebSocket API contract is defined in `/docs/api-reference/client-messages` and `/docs/api-reference/server-events`.
- The transcript state machine contract is defined in `/docs/realtime/transcript-lifecycle` and `/docs/concepts/stablestream`.
- LiveFinal™ behavior and availability are described in `/docs/concepts/livefinal`. `transcript.revision` is currently `0`; correction occurs before the single completed event when refinement is enabled. There is no separate public correction event or session-wide final event on the documented Realtime endpoint.
- Raw Markdown for any page: `https://docs.lansonai.com/raw/docs/<path>.md` (e.g. `/raw/docs/start/quickstart.md`).
- The Recorded API OpenAPI spec at `https://audio.lansonai.com/openapi.json` is the schema-accurate source for recorded endpoints.
